hook: Hyderabad unsold homes up *7%*; sales rose only 3%
hook_b: Hyderabad unsold homes up *7%*; sales rose only 3%
tldr: Knight Frank India says new launches stayed ahead of sales in Q3 2026, so Hyderabad's unsold inventory rose 7% while average sales rose 3%.

beats.what: Quarters to Sell (QTS) rose from 5.8 quarters in Q3 2025 to 6.1 quarters in Q3 2026.
beats.why: New project launches continued to outpace demand, Knight Frank said.
beats.care: Homebuyers face a market with more unsold stock on the shelf.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Across India's top eight markets, average QTS also edged up to 6.1 quarters from an eight-year low of 5.8; it was 7-11 quarters between 2018 and 2021.

cards.q: More unsold homes: what should change first?

qs: Will slower absorption push developers to cut prices or slow launches?

facts.t: India's top markets took *7-11 quarters* to clear stock in 2018-21, versus 6.1 now.

viz.verdict: Unsold homes take longer to clear; tougher for developers, more choice for buyers.

learn.t: QTS = Quarters to Sell, time to clear unsold stock at the last eight quarters' sales rate

watch: Whether developers slow new launches in the coming quarters.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: Unsold housing inventory rises 7 per cent in Hyderabad

fact: Hyderabad's unsold housing stock rose *7%* as launches outpaced sales
twist: At current pace it would take *1.52 years* to sell the stock, up from 1.45 years.
